source_note: Values are sourced from the SF32 Family comparison and quick-selection tables (sf32-products/family/SF32_family.md) plus each chip's own 'Family Variants' package/memory table. Camera and AI-accelerator flags reflect only what that page explicitly states per family -- absence of a flag means it isn't documented there, not a confirmed 'no'. Package type reflects literal package-option membership per part (a family listing both QFN68 and BGA options matches both); 'QFN80' is a distinct package_types value used only by the SF32LB57xY tier, since its footprint (8 x 8 mm) and GPIO count differ from QFN68 (7 x 7 mm). Power flags: 'Li-ion' means the part has a documented 3.2-4.7V direct-battery rail; '1.8V' means the part's documented supply range goes down to ~1.71V or is a fixed 1.8V rail; '3.3V' means the part has a genuine, separately-documented externally-regulated 3.3V supply option -- NOT simply that 3.3V is numerically within a battery-input range (e.g. SF32LB523U/525U/527U run on a raw 3.2-4.7V battery rail with no 3.3V-supply variant, so they are Li-ion-only despite 3.3V sitting inside that range). Target resolution uses total pixel count as a capacity proxy, not a guarantee of exact aspect-ratio or interface compatibility -- always confirm against the target chip's own datasheet before committing a design. SF32LB52x, SF32LB55x, SF32LB56x, SF32LB57x, and SF32LB58x are split into their orderable package/memory tiers (e.g. SF32LB525U, SF32LB555V4O6/555V436/557VD3A6, SF32LB566V, SF32LB57xU/V/Y, SF32LB583V) rather than one blended family row. Where a chip page's per-tier table did not break out PSRAM/Flash by package (SF32LB57x), all tiers inherit the family-wide memory ceiling rather than a fabricated per-package number. display_interfaces omits SPI and 8080, since every catalogued part documents both and they carry no selection-relevant information; psram_max_mb is always a numeric total (used for the Minimum PSRAM filter), and psram_label additionally states the per-channel split as 'N + N MB' for the documented dual-channel/dual-pool parts (SF32LB557VD3A6, SF32LB566V, SF32LB583V, SF32LB586V, SF32LB587V) so the table doesn't imply one contiguous pool where the datasheet actually documents two independent ones. audio_dac/audio_adc/audio_pdm/audio_i2s are sourced from SF32_family.md's Audio ADC/DAC/PDM/I2S Interfaces comparison row and are uniform across every part within a family (audio capability is a whole-die feature, not something SiFli's docs vary by package or memory tier), with one confirmed exception: SF32LB55x's own per-part-number table (DS5501-SF32LB55x datasheet, 'Table 0-1: SF32LB55x Product Series') shows I2S and PDM count tied to the same HCPU+LCPU split that varies by package -- QFN68L/BGA145 (SF32LB551/553/555, including our SF32LB555V4O6 and SF32LB555V436) each have 1x I2S + 1x PDM, while only BGA169 (SF32LB557, our SF32LB557VD3A6) has 2x I2S + 2x PDM; the two BGA145 records were corrected from the previously blended 2x/2x to the package-correct 1x/1x. The Audio filter matches on a per-dimension minimum threshold (each of DAC/ADC/PDM/I2S must be greater than or equal to the selected preset's value) rather than an exact-profile match, consistent with how the PSRAM and GPIO filters already work -- a part with more of everything than a given preset still qualifies for it, even if its exact combination isn't one of the catalogued presets itself. SF32LB52BU (external-3.3V, NOR-flash-only, no PSRAM) was added alongside the other SF32LB52x tiers from the same chip-page variant table. SF32LB55x was split into SF32LB555V4O6 (BGA145, 4MB PSRAM, 4MB NOR boot flash), SF32LB555V436 (BGA145, 8MB PSRAM, 4MB NOR boot flash), and SF32LB557VD3A6 (BGA169, 16+2MB dual-pool PSRAM, 1MB NOR boot flash), sourced from the SiFli chip model guide's per-part-number table (wiki.sifli.com/silicon, '芯片型号指南', SF32LB55x section) rather than SF32LB55x.md's own package-level GPIO table, because that source gives an explicit HCPU+LCPU GPIO count and per-part memory breakdown that SF32LB55x.md's page does not. This surfaced one real cross-document discrepancy worth flagging: SF32LB55x.md's package table states BGA169 = 119 GPIO, while the model guide's SF32LB557VD3A6-specific row gives 71 HCPU + 42 LCPU = 113 GPIO; the more specific, part-numbered source (113) was used here. The model guide's per-part table also shows display interfaces vary by package for SF32LB55x specifically -- QFN68L-package parts (not catalogued here) get QSPI/8080 only, BGA145 parts add MIPI, and JDI/Sharp-MIP support is documented only for SF32LB557VD3A6 -- so 'RGB', which appears in SF32_family.md's coarser cross-family comparison row for SF32LB55x, is omitted from all three split records pending confirmation, since neither the model guide's per-part table nor SF32LB55x.md's own Graphics feature list documents an RGB/DPI interface for this family. Max resolution for all three SF32LB55x BGA tiers (SF32LB555V4O6, SF32LB555V436, SF32LB557VD3A6) is set to 640x480 per direct confirmation from the μForge product team. audio_pdm for all SF32LB52x-family records (chips, module, and devkits) was corrected from 2x to 1x per the official SF32LB52x datasheet (DS5201-SF32LB52x, V2.5.3) -- both its 'Peripherals and I/Os' feature-bullet list ('1x PDM') and its hardware design guide independently confirm 1x, contradicting SF32_family.md's cross-family comparison table, which had incorrectly listed SF32LB52x as 2x (also corrected). This gave SF32LB52x its own distinct audio profile (1x ADC + 1x DAC + 1x PDM + 1x I2S), which did not previously exist as a preset in the Audio dropdown; a fifth preset option was added for it. audio_pdm for all SF32LB58x-family records (chips, module, and devkit) was corrected from 4x to 2x per the official SF32LB58x datasheet (DS5801-SF32LB58x, V1.8.3), which states '2x PDM' in three independent places (the headline Audio feature bullets, the I/O Peripherals bullets, and the peripheral address map, which lists exactly two PDM instances -- PDM1 and PDM2, with no third or fourth). SF32LB58x.md's own feature-bullet list had independently drifted to '4x PDM microphone inputs' (also corrected), while its hardware design guide had already correctly stated 2x throughout -- so the error was isolated to the top-line feature summaries (SF32_family.md and SF32LB58x.md), not the design-level documentation. This changed SF32LB58x's audio profile from 2x ADC + 2x DAC + 4x PDM + 3x I2S to 2x ADC + 2x DAC + 2x PDM + 3x I2S; since no other family used the old 4x-PDM profile, the existing 'audioD' dropdown preset was updated in place rather than adding a new option. free_io and ptm flags were added for FreeIO (flexible GPIO assignment) and PTM (Peripheral Task Machine, a 4-core parallel task engine for deterministic-timing peripheral offload), both sourced from sf32-products/chips/SF32LB57x.md's feature bullets and its dedicated 'PTM Peripheral Task Machine' subsection. A sitewide search confirmed both features are documented exclusively for SF32LB57x -- SF32LB52x.md, SF32LB55x.md, SF32LB56x.md, SF32LB58x.md, and SF32_family.md's comparison table make no mention of FreeIO for any family, and PTM appears only in SF32LB57x's own row -- so free_io and ptm are true only for the three SF32LB57xU/V/Y records and false for every other part. ai_accelerator was corrected from false to true for all three SF32LB55x records (SF32LB555V4O6, SF32LB555V436, SF32LB557VD3A6) and all SF32LB56x-family records (SF32LB566V, SF32LB567V, SF32LB56-MOD, SF32LB56-DevKit-LCD), per each chip's own 'Graphics, Display, and AI' section, which documents a 'Neural-network matrix accelerator for TinyML workloads' for both families (1.92GOPS/5.73TOPS/W for 55x, 1.92GOPS/>10TOPS/W for 56x) -- SF32_family.md's coarser comparison table doesn't call this out per-family the way the individual chip pages do, which is why it had been missed originally. SF32LB52x.md and SF32LB57x.md document no equivalent accelerator, so those families remain ai_accelerator: false. wifi (external Wi-Fi via SDIO) was corrected from false to true for SF32LB52BU and for all three SF32LB55x records (SF32LB555V4O6, SF32LB555V436, SF32LB557VD3A6) and all three SF32LB57x records (SF32LB57xU/V/Y), per direct confirmation from the μForge product team -- unlike SF32LB56x and SF32LB58x, whose own chip pages explicitly state 'External Wi-Fi connectivity through SDIO', SF32LB52x.md, SF32LB55x.md, and SF32LB57x.md don't spell this out per-part, so this correction relies on the product team's direct confirmation rather than a chip-page citation; the other SF32LB52x tiers (523U/525U/527U/52JU/52DU) were not included in this correction and remain wifi: false pending the same confirmation. Chip-tier 'name' fields were updated to show the complete orderable postfix (package/memory suffix) instead of the bare family-plus-power-suffix form, sourced from each chip's own hardware design guide or product page order-code table: SF32LB523U -> SF32LB523UB6, SF32LB525U -> SF32LB525UC6, SF32LB527U -> SF32LB527UD6, SF32LB52JU -> SF32LB52JUD6, and SF32LB52DU -> SF32LB52DUB6 (all four from SF32LB52x_hardware_design_guide.md's power-variant tables); SF32LB566V -> SF32LB566VCB36 and SF32LB567V -> SF32LB567VND36 (from SF32LB56x.md's orderable-parts table); SF32LB583V -> SF32LB583VCC36, SF32LB586V -> SF32LB586VDD36, and SF32LB587V -> SF32LB587VEE56 (from SF32LB58x.md's orderable-parts table). SF32LB55x records already carried their complete postfix and were untouched. The SF32LB52BU record originally blended two distinct orderable SKUs (SF32LB52BU36 with 1MB flash and SF32LB52BU56 with 4MB flash) under one row and was initially left unpostfixed for that reason; per explicit direction, it was subsequently split to represent SF32LB52BU36 specifically, and flash_max_mb (4 -> 1), power_1v8 (false -> true, since SF32LB52BU36's VDD_SIP accepts either 1.8V or 3.3V per SF32LB52x_hardware_design_guide.md's power-variant table, unlike SF32LB52BU56 which requires 3.3V only), power_supply, and summary were corrected to match that specific SKU rather than the blended pair. SF32LB52BU56 itself is not separately catalogued here. The three SF32LB57x records (SF32LB57xU/V/Y) remain unpostfixed and use the family's own lowercase-x package/power-tier placeholder convention (matching the labeling already used in SF32LB57x.md's Family Variants table), since SF32LB57x.md's own documentation only gives example orderable part numbers (e.g. SF32LB573UB7N6 -- see the SF32LB57x datasheet's ordering-information table) that don't cleanly map one-to-one onto the three generic package/power tiers listed here. Six digital-peripheral count fields were added -- uart, i2c, spi, can, gpadc_channels, usb -- sourced per family (uniform across every part in that family, same convention as the audio fields) from each chip's own 'Peripherals and I/Os' bullets on its product page, cross-checked against the CAN and USB rows of SF32_family.md's SF32 Microcontroller Comparison table: SF32LB52x = 3 UART / 4 I2C / 2 SPI / 0 CAN / 1 USB (2.0 FS); SF32LB55x = 5 UART / 6 I2C / 4 SPI / 0 CAN / 1 USB (2.0 FS), GPADC channel count of 8 from its own product page ('1x 10-bit general-purpose SAR ADC, 8 channels'); SF32LB56x = 6 UART / 7 I2C / 4 SPI / 1 CAN / 1 USB (2.0 FS), GPADC channel count of 8 from its own product page ('1x 12-bit general-purpose SAR ADC, 8 channels'); SF32LB57x = 3 UART / 4 I2C / 2 SPI / 2 CAN / 1 USB (2.0 FS), GPADC channel count of 12 confirmed against SF32LB57x_hardware_design_guide.md's GPADC pin-assignment table (GPADC_CH0-CH10 on PA28-PA38 plus VBAT/VBATS as GPADC_CH11); SF32LB58x = 2 CAN (from its own 'Peripherals and I/Os' bullet '2x CAN interfaces', matching SF32_family.md) and 1 USB (2.0 HS). SF32LB58x's uart/i2c/spi are null (not 0) because no page states an exact UART/I2C/SPI interface count for this family -- its own product page only lists '6 selectable UART debug outputs' (a debug-pin count, not a UART peripheral count) and a generic, uncounted 'I2C, SPI' mention -- so these were left unconfirmed rather than guessed. gpadc_channels is likewise null for SF32LB52x and SF32LB58x: neither family's product page or hardware design guide states an exact GPADC channel count or includes a GPADC pin-assignment table like SF32LB57x's, unlike SF32LB55x and SF32LB56x, which state the channel count directly in their own 'Peripherals and I/Os' bullets. All five null cells render as 'n/a' in the table rather than a fabricated number. Correction: SF32LB52x's gpadc_channels was initially left null pending further sourcing, but SF32LB52-MOD-1_hardware_design_guide.md (built on the SF32LB525UC6 die, same silicon as the bare SF32LB52x chip) states explicitly: '12-bit GPADC -- SAR ADC, ... 7 single-ended channels + 1 battery-voltage channel (or 3 differential pairs) ...' -- 7 GPIO-exposed channels (GPADC_CH1-CH7 on PA28/PA29/PA30/PA31/PA32/PA33/PA34 per that same guide's pin table) plus 1 dedicated VBAT channel (confirmed separately by SF32LB52x_hardware_design_guide.md: 'the VBAT pin, which has an integrated GPADC channel') = 8 total, the same GPIO-channels+1 pattern as SF32LB57x (11 + 1 VBAT = 12). gpadc_channels for all SF32LB52x-family records updated from null to 8. SF32LB58x's gpadc_channels remains null -- no equivalent channel count or pin-table breakdown was found in any SF32LB58x chip, module, or design-guide page. Reordered the SF32LB57x tier rows so SF32LB57xY (QFN80) now sits above SF32LB57xV (BGA112), between SF32LB57xU and SF32LB57xV, at the user's request -- no data values changed, display order only. Removed the 6 devkit-tier records (SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD, SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3, SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano, SF32LB52-DevKit-ULP, SF32LB56-DevKit-LCD, SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD) from the selection table at the user's request -- the tool is now scoped to chips and modules only. The 'Development board' tier-filter option was removed from product-selector.js accordingly. Correction: SF32LB58x's uart/i2c/spi/gpadc_channels were left null pending further sourcing, but SF32LB58-MOD_hardware_design_guide.md (built on the SF32LB586VDD36 die, same silicon as the bare SF32LB58x chip) states explicitly under its Peripherals section: 'UART -- ... UART1-3 are on HPSYS; UART4-6 are on LPSYS' (6 total, corroborated by SF32LB58x_hardware_design_guide.md's own debug-UART pin table listing TXD1/RXD1 through TXD6/RXD6); 'I2C -- ... I2C1-4 are on HPSYS; I2C5-7 are on LPSYS' (7 total); 'SPI -- ... SPI1/2 are on HPSYS (max 48MHz); SPI3/4 are on LPSYS (max 24MHz)' (4 total); '12-bit GPADC -- SAR ADC, ... 8 single-ended channels (or 4 differential pairs) ...' (8 total; unlike SF32LB52x/57x, no separate VBAT-GPADC channel is documented anywhere for SF32LB58x, consistent with SF32LB58x not offering a direct Li-ion battery rail in this dataset, so no +1 was added here). uart/i2c/spi/gpadc_channels for all SF32LB58x-family records updated from null to 6/7/4/8 respectively. Added an io_voltage field per record (the chip's GPIO/VDDIO supply rail range, distinct from the existing power_supply field which covers the main VBAT/PVDD system-power input). Sourced from each chip's own Power Supply Requirements table: SF32LB52x regular-powered variants (52BU/52JU/52DU) and SF32LB55x use VDDIOA/VDDIOB = 1.71-3.63V (52x's typ column lists 1.8/3.3V dual; 55x's typ column lists 1.8V only, though the same 3.63V max applies); SF32LB56x and SF32LB58x chips use VDDIOA/VDDIOA2/VDDIOB = 1.71-3.45V (typ 1.8V). SF32LB57x splits by power family per its own Table 5.2-5 'Key Power-Family Differences': 3.3V-supply variants (57xV, 57xY) have VDDIOA supplied by the external 3.3V rail (io_voltage = 3.3V fixed), while the battery-powered variant (57xU) has no documented VDDIOA voltage table at all -- left null. The same applies to SF32LB52x's battery-powered chip variants (523U/525U/527U) and to SF32LB52-MOD-1 (built on that same battery-powered die): no VDDIOA table exists in their design guides, only internal LDOs not intended to power ordinary GPIO, so io_voltage is left null (n/a) for these four records rather than guessed. SF32LB56-MOD and SF32LB58-MOD use their own module-level datasheet VDDIO spec (1.7-3.6V) rather than the bare chip's table, since the module's own datasheet is the more authoritative source for that specific product; both modules also note that PA00-PA11 are hardwired to 3.3V regardless of the VDDIO setting, which the table doesn't capture. Correction: SF32LB523U/525U/527U and SF32LB52-MOD-1 (battery-powered SF32LB52x die) were left null for io_voltage on the assumption that no GPIO supply rail was documented, but SF32LB52-MOD-1_hardware_design_guide.md (built on the SF32LB525UC6 die, same silicon) states explicitly in its electrical-notes section: 'The module's IO interface level is 3.3V -- any peripheral connected must also use 3.3V logic levels,' with 'VDD is the I/O supply rail' clarifying that this is a fixed 3.3V rail (from the internal VDD33_VOUT2 LDO) rather than an externally flexible VDDIOA range like the regular-powered 52B/D/E/G/J variants have -- which is also why no VDDIOA min/typ/max table exists for this power family. io_voltage updated from null to 3.3V for all four battery-powered SF32LB52x records. Changed the usb field from a plain count (always 1) to a speed-qualified label -- '1xFS' or '1xHS' -- per the user's request to distinguish USB2.0 Full-Speed from High-Speed. Sourced per family from each chip's own product page: SF32LB52x ('1x USB2.0 FS'), SF32LB55x ('1x USB2.0 FS Host/Device'), SF32LB56x ('1x USB2.0 FS'), and SF32LB57x ('1x USB 2.0 Full-Speed') are all FS-only; SF32LB58x ('USB2.0 High-Speed Host/Device') is HS-only, corroborated by SF32_family.md's comparison table (USB row: '2.0 FS' for 52x/55x/56x/57x, '2.0 HS' for 58x). No family documents both an FS and an HS port together, so no record uses the '1xFS+1xHS' combined form -- the table/filter code supports it if a future part needs it. Relabeled io_voltage from the raw '1.71-3.63V' datasheet min/max range to '3.3V/1.8V' for SF32LB52BU/52JU/52DU and the SF32LB55x records, at the user's request -- this matches the two nominal operating levels the VDDIOA/VDDIOB rail is actually run at in practice (1.8V or 3.3V), rather than the full electrical tolerance band, and is consistent with how the existing Power supply column already displays nominal levels (e.g. '1.8V / 3.3V') instead of raw min/max voltages. Relabeled io_voltage from raw min/max ranges ('1.71-3.45V' for the SF32LB56x/SF32LB58x chip records, '1.7-3.6V' for the SF32LB56-MOD/SF32LB58-MOD module records) to '3.3V/1.8V', same treatment and rationale as the earlier '1.71-3.63V' relabeling -- all of these ranges represent the same VDDIOA/VDDIO rail run at one of the two nominal levels (1.8V or 3.3V) in practice, so the whole io_voltage column now consistently shows nominal levels rather than raw electrical tolerance bands, matching the Power supply column's style. Replaced the three generic SF32LB57x tier-placeholder rows (57xU/57xY/57xV) with confirmed real orderable part numbers per user-supplied SF32LB57x ordering-table data, and split each QFN68/QFN80 tier into its battery-powered and (where applicable) 3.3V-supply SKU variants rather than one blended generic row: SF32LB573UB7N6 (QFN68, battery, 4MB OPI-PSRAM + 16MB QSPI-NOR Flash, 46 GPIO per SF32LB57x.md's battery-QFN68 GPIO count) replaces the old generic 57xU row and matches the site's own pre-existing SF32LB57x.md orderable-examples entry for the same part number/memory combo. SF32LB577UDNN6 (QFN68, battery, 16MB OPI-PSRAM, no in-package Flash, 46 GPIO) is a newly added second battery-QFN68 SKU. SF32LB57EYBBN6 (QFN80, external 3.3V supply, same 8MB dual-pool PSRAM and no-Flash configuration as 575Y, 58 GPIO) is the newly added 3.3V-supply counterpart, with io_voltage = 3.3V per the same 'VDDIOA supplied by external 3.3V' rule already established for SF32LB57xV/57xY. All four battery-powered records among these (573U/577U/575Y) have power_supply narrowed to the pure battery range (3.2-4.7V, removing the earlier blended '/ 2.97-3.63V' text) since each is now a specific confirmed battery-only SKU rather than a generic tier spanning both power families. Flash values of 0 (not null) reflect that these specific SKUs are confirmed to have no in-package NOR Flash at all (per the ordering-table descriptions listing only PSRAM), distinct from null which means undocumented/unknown. The BGA112 row (SF32LB57xV) is unchanged -- no real orderable part number for it has been supplied yet. Simplified the usb field labels from '1xFS'/'1xHS' to 'FS'/'HS' (dropping the '1x' count prefix, since USB port count isn't the point of this field) at the user's request; a part with both a Full-Speed and a High-Speed port would use 'FS+HS', though no current SF32 family documents both together. Added three more confirmed real SF32LB57x orderable part numbers per user-supplied data: SF32LB57ZUN3N6 (QFN68, 3.3V-supply -- 'Z' is one of the '57Z/C/E/F/G/H/J' 3.3V-supply tier letters already documented in SF32LB57x_hardware_design_guide.md's power-family table -- with no in-package PSRAM and 1MB/8Mb Flash only, decoded from the 'N3' memory code where 'N' as the first (PSRAM) position is read the same way 'N' was already established to mean 'none' in the second (Flash) position for SF32LB577UDNN6); SF32LB573UB776 (QFN68, battery, same 4MB PSRAM + 16MB Flash configuration as the already-added SF32LB573UB7N6 -- the two part numbers share an identical 'B7' memory code and differ only in the final suffix character (7 vs N), whose meaning isn't confirmed by any site documentation, so both are kept as distinct rows with identical specs rather than merged or guessed apart); SF32LB57GYD7N6 (QFN80, 3.3V-supply -- 'G' is likewise one of the 57x 3.3V-supply tier letters -- 16MB PSRAM + 16MB Flash, decoded from the 'D7' memory code). All four use the GPIO counts already established per package/power-family from SF32LB57x.md's Package and Power Overview table (QFN68 battery = 46, QFN68 3.3V-supply = 47, QFN80 = 58), and the 'io_voltage = 3.3V for 3.3V-supply variants, null for battery-powered ones' rule already established for the rest of the SF32LB57x family. Correction: SF32LB57x's io_voltage was previously derived from the power family (3.3V for 3.3V-supply variants, null/unconfirmed for battery-powered ones), but per the user's direct clarification, io_voltage for this family actually depends on PACKAGE, not power family: QFN68 (57xU-suffix parts) supports 3.3V IO only, while QFN80 (57xY-suffix) and BGA112 (57xV-suffix) support both 3.3V and 1.8V IO. io_voltage updated accordingly for every SF32LB57x record: all QFN68 parts (SF32LB573UB7N6, SF32LB577UDNN6, SF32LB57ZUN3N6, SF32LB573UB776) = '3.3V'; all QFN80 parts (SF32LB57EYBBN6, SF32LB57GYD7N6) and the BGA112 part (SF32LB57xV) = '3.3V/1.8V'. This also resolves the earlier battery-powered-QFN68 null/n/a gap (SF32LB573UB7N6, SF32LB577UDNN6, SF32LB573UB776 no longer show n/a for this column). Sorted the SF32LB57x QFN68 (57xU) rows into tier order: numeric battery-tier digits ascending first (SF32LB573UB7N6, SF32LB573UB776, SF32LB577UDNN6), then alphabetic 3.3V-supply tier letters (SF32LB57ZUN3N6), per the user's requested ordering convention -- lower numbers before higher numbers, then letters alphabetically. Correction: SF32LB573UB776's Flash capacity was initially set to 16MB (misreading its 'B776' memory code the same way as SF32LB573UB7N6's 'B7N6'), but the user confirmed it should be 32MB. Re-examining the code: the repeated digit '77' (rather than '7N') follows the same dual-die convention already established for PSRAM codes like 'BB' (SF32LB57EYBBN6's repeated PSRAM letter meaning two same-capacity dies, summed) -- so '77' means two 128Mb (16MB) Flash dies = 32MB total, not a single 16MB die. Added a flash_label field (mirroring the existing psram_label convention) so the table shows '16 + 16 MB' instead of the summed '32 MB' alone, making the dual-die configuration visible the same way dual-pool PSRAM already is. flash_max_mb corrected from 16 to 32. Reordered same-tier-digit SF32LB57x QFN68 rows (573U variants) by total memory ascending -- SF32LB573UB7N6 (4MB PSRAM + 16MB Flash = 20MB total) now sits above SF32LB573UB776 (4MB PSRAM + 32MB Flash = 36MB total), per the user's tie-break rule: when two rows share the same tier digit/letter within a package group, the one with less total memory sorts above the one with more. Added SF32LB57GVD776 (BGA112, 3.3V-supply -- 'G' is the same 3.3V-supply tier letter already used for SF32LB57GYD7N6 -- with 16MB PSRAM and 32MB (2x 16MB dual-die) Flash, decoded from the 'D776' memory code using the same rules already established: 'D' = 128Mb/16MB PSRAM, and the repeated '77' Flash digit = two 128Mb/16MB Flash dies summed, same as SF32LB573UB776). io_voltage = '3.3V/1.8V' per the package-based rule (BGA112 supports both). Inserted directly above the still-generic SF32LB57xV placeholder row. Removed the generic SF32LB57xV BGA112 tier-placeholder row at the user's request, now that SF32LB57GVD776 gives a confirmed real orderable BGA112 part number -- no more generic, un-postfixed SF32LB57x placeholder rows remain. Added two more confirmed real SF32LB57x QFN68 part numbers per user-supplied data: SF32LB573UB766 and SF32LB575UCNN6. Decoding SF32LB573UB766 required generalizing the dual-Flash-die rule discovered from SF32LB573UB776's correction -- rather than requiring the two Flash-digit slots to match (dual-same-capacity), the general rule is that each digit slot is summed independently using the SF32_namingrule.md Flash legend, so '76' = 128Mb (16MB) + 64Mb (8MB) = 24MB total, shown via flash_label as '16 + 8 MB'. SF32LB575UCNN6 decodes straightforwardly from the already-established 'single PSRAM letter + NN = no Flash' pattern (same as SF32LB577UDNN6), giving 8MB PSRAM (C) and 0MB Flash. Both inserted into the QFN68 group in total-memory ascending order per the user's established same-tier-digit ordering rule: SF32LB573UB766 (28MB total) sits between SF32LB573UB7N6 (20MB) and SF32LB573UB776 (36MB); SF32LB575UCNN6 (8MB total) sits first in the group. Correction: SF32LB57GVD776's gpio_max was set to 64 based on the generic BGA112 package assumption inherited from the old SF32LB57xV placeholder, but the user confirmed this specific SKU has 58 GPIOs, not 64. Updated accordingly -- the BGA112 package's 64-GPIO figure in SF32LB57x.md's Package and Power Overview table apparently doesn't apply uniformly to every real BGA112 orderable part. Clarification on SF32LB57x BGA112 GPIO counts, per the user: the package's GPIO count depends on what occupies the second in-package memory slot. Dual-PSRAM configurations (PSRAM in that second slot) have 58 GPIOs. Configurations without PSRAM in that slot (a second Flash die, or no second die) have 64 total GPIO-capable pins, but 6 of those are dedicated to MPI3 (for routing the second Flash die) and are not general-purpose reassignable GPIO, so they should not be counted as 6 additional usable GPIOs. SF32LB57GVD776 (single PSRAM + dual-die Flash, i.e. Flash rather than PSRAM in the second slot) keeps gpio_max = 58 to reflect genuinely general-purpose I/O, not the raw 64-pin count that includes its 6 MPI3-only pins. Added an sdio field (count of independent SD/SDIO/eMMC controllers) per family: SF32LB52x = 1 ('1x SD3.0/SDIO3.0/eMMC' on its own product page, confirmed 1x on SF32LB52-MOD-1's own storage table); SF32LB56x = 2 ('2x SD/SDIO/eMMC, one 4-bit and one 8-bit' on its own product page, confirmed via SF32LB56-MOD's SDMMC1/SDMMC2 description); SF32LB57x = 2 ('2x SD/SDIO interfaces' on its own product page); SF32LB58x = 2 ('dual SD1/SD2 SDIO interfaces', explicitly stated multiple times in its hardware design guide, confirmed via SF32LB58-MOD's own SD1/SD2 pin table); SF32LB55x = 2, inferred from its hardware design guide's three SDIO pin tables (5.5-7/5.5-8/5.5-9, 'Interface 1/2/3') -- Interface 1 and Interface 2 share identical CLK/CMD/DATA0-3 pin assignments and differ only in whether DATA4-7 are added, meaning they document one controller's 4-bit vs 8-bit wiring options rather than two separate controllers (a chip cannot route two independent controllers onto the same physical pins simultaneously), while Interface 3 uses an entirely different pin group and is therefore a genuinely separate second controller -- no prose statement on SF32LB55x's pages gives an explicit numeric count, so this figure is inferred from the pin-table evidence rather than directly stated. Reordered so each family's module-tier row (SF32LB52-MOD-1, SF32LB56-MOD, SF32LB58-MOD) sits as the last row within its own family's block, instead of all modules being grouped together at the very end of the table. Renamed the SF32LB52-MOD-1 product-selector record to its specific orderable SKU, SF32LB52-MOD-1-N16R8, matching the module page's own Module Variants table (this is the module's only listed variant), and corrected that record's psram_max_mb/flash_max_mb which had been swapped (now 8MB PSRAM / 16MB NOR Flash, matching both the doc table and the N16R8 suffix). Renamed the SF32LB56-MOD product-selector record to the SF32LB56-MOD-N16R12N1 SKU (one of three variants on the module page's own Memory and Module Variants table), and corrected its psram_max_mb/flash_max_mb, which had been swapped and matched neither the old generic name nor any real variant (now 12MB PSRAM = 4+8MB dual-channel OPI-PSRAM, 17MB total Flash = 16MB main + 1MB backup QSPI-NOR, per the doc table). Renamed the SF32LB58-MOD product-selector record to the SF32LB58-MOD-N16R32N1 SKU (one of three variants on the module page's own Memory and Module Variants table), and corrected its psram_max_mb (was 64, wrong) / flash_max_mb (was 8, wrong) to 32MB PSRAM = 16+16MB dual-channel HPI-PSRAM, 17MB total Flash = 16MB main + 1MB backup QSPI-NOR, per the doc table. Added two more SF32LB58-MOD memory variants alongside the previously documented SF32LB58-MOD-N16R32N1: SF32LB58-MOD-N16R16N1 (16MB main QSPI-NOR + 16MB HPI-PSRAM + 1MB backup QSPI-NOR) and SF32LB58-MOD-N16R64N4 (16MB main QSPI-NOR + 64MB HPI-PSRAM + 4MB backup QSPI-NOR). These two are not yet listed in SF32LB58-MOD.md's own Memory and Module Variants table -- their memory figures are inferred from the established SF32LB58-MOD/SF32LB56-MOD order-code convention (N<main flash MB>R<PSRAM MB>N<backup flash MB>), not from independent per-channel PSRAM documentation, so psram_label is left null (unconfirmed split) rather than guessing e.g. a symmetric 8+8MB/32+32MB breakdown the way N16R32N1's real 16+16MB was confirmed. All other specs (package, peripherals, power, display) are assumed identical to N16R32N1 since these are memory-only SKU variants of the same physical module. Corrected SF32LB58-MOD-N16R16N1 and SF32LB58-MOD-N16R64N4's PSRAM labels from unconfirmed nulls to confirmed per-channel splits, per direct correction: N16R32N1 is based on SF32LB586VDD36, N16R64N4 is based on SF32LB587VEE56 -- and by the same exact-match pattern (PSRAM total and in-package Flash total both matching), N16R16N1 is based on SF32LB583VCC36. Their psram_label values (8+8MB, 32+32MB) now come directly from those confirmed base chips' own records rather than being guessed, and SF32LB583V/SF32LB587V's links.closest_module were updated to point at SF32LB58-MOD.md to match SF32LB586V's existing cross-link. Removed SF32LB58-MOD-E4R32N1 from the product-selector table and the module's own variant table, and generalized the three N16-flavor SF32LB58-MOD module summaries/page prose to describe the module as based on the SF32LB58x family generally rather than naming a specific member chip (SF32LB586VDD36 etc.), per direct correction -- the module line spans the 583/586/587 family, not one chip. Corrected all three SF32LB58-MOD variants' gpio_max from 154 (the bare SF32LB58x chip's own GPIO count, wrongly carried over) to 103, counted directly from SF32LB58-MOD_hardware_design_guide.md's Table 4.2-1 Pin Definition Table: of the module's 138 physical pins, 103 list a GPIO_xxx alternate function and 35 are power/ground/analog-audio/MIPI-DSI/USB/BT-antenna pins with no GPIO capability. The module does not expose every chip GPIO -- some are consumed internally or simply not routed to the module's own pins, same as every other SF32 module (SF32LB52-MOD-1: 45 of 68; per direct correction, this class of module-vs-chip GPIO gap applies here too). Source-check follow-up (2026-10-07): corrected SF32LB52BU36 main-supply metadata: PVDD is 2.97-3.63V (nominal 3.3V); the SKU-specific external 1.8V-or-3.3V note is for VDD_SIP, not the main rail, so power_1v8 is false. This supersedes the earlier catalog note that treated the VDD_SIP option as main-supply support. Corrected the three SF32LB58x chip records to 160 GPIOs (94 HCPU + 66 LCPU) per the current Chip Model Guide; module records remain 103 exposed GPIO_xxx pins. Retained SF32LB55x 640x480 as the existing product-team-confirmed conservative selector value; the official 55x Product Brief documents display interfaces and frame rate but no numeric maximum resolution. Retained SF32LB58x 1280x720 as a conservative pixel-capacity screening value: the 58x Product Brief reports 1024x1024 in its Graphics/Display section, and the 58-DevKit guide demonstrates up to 1280x800 on the 586-based board; that board-level result is not generalized to every SKU.

parts.name: SF32LB523UB6
parts.summary: Battery-powered QFN68 tier with 4MB OPI-PSRAM -- compact graphics headroom above the base 520 SKU.

parts.name: SF32LB525UC6
parts.summary: Battery-powered QFN68 tier with 8MB OPI-PSRAM -- the standard chip used by SF32LB52-MOD-1 and SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD.

parts.name: SF32LB527UD6
parts.summary: Battery-powered QFN68 tier with 16MB OPI-PSRAM -- the largest memory option in the battery-powered group.

parts.name: SF32LB52BU36
parts.summary: External-supply QFN68 tier with 1MB SPI/QSPI-NOR Flash only, no PSRAM -- VDD_SIP accepts an external 1.8V or 3.3V supply, unlike the 4MB SF32LB52BU56 variant, which requires 3.3V.

parts.name: SF32LB52JUD6
parts.summary: External 3.3V-supply QFN68 tier with 16MB OPI-PSRAM -- the largest memory option in the standard external-supply group; not pin compatible with the battery-powered group.

parts.name: SF32LB52DUB6
parts.summary: Special ultra-low-power 1.8V-supply QFN68 tier with 4MB OPI-PSRAM -- electrically distinct from the 3.3V external-supply group.

parts.name: SF32LB52-MOD-1-N16R8
parts.summary: SF32LB525UC6-based Bluetooth module with module-level antenna, lowering RF and certification risk versus a chip-down SF32LB52x design.

parts.name: SF32LB555V4O6
parts.summary: BGA145 tier with 4MB OPI-PSRAM and 4MB NOR boot flash -- the smaller-memory BGA145 option in the BLE-only mainstream family.

parts.name: SF32LB555V436
parts.summary: BGA145 tier with 8MB OPI-PSRAM and 4MB NOR boot flash -- same package and GPIO count as SF32LB555V4O6, with double the PSRAM.

parts.name: SF32LB557VD3A6
parts.summary: BGA169 tier with 16MB+2MB dual-pool PSRAM (18MB total), 1MB NOR boot flash, and the family's only JDI/Sharp MIP display support -- the highest-I/O and highest-memory SF32LB55x tier.

parts.name: SF32LB566VCB36
parts.summary: WBBGA175 tier with 8MB+4MB dual-pool OPI-PSRAM and 1MB QSPI-NOR flash -- the exact silicon used by SF32LB56-MOD and SF32LB56-DevKit-LCD.

parts.name: SF32LB567VND36
parts.summary: WBBGA175 tier with a larger 16MB single-pool OPI-PSRAM and 1MB QSPI-NOR flash, for designs that prioritize single-pool memory over the module's standard 566V chip.

parts.name: SF32LB56-MOD-N16R12N1
parts.summary: SF32LB56xV-based general-purpose module with BLE Audio, richer graphics/audio/storage options, and PCB or IPEX antenna variants.

parts.name: SF32LB573UB7N6
parts.summary: QFN68 battery-powered tier with 4MB OPI-PSRAM and 16MB QSPI-NOR Flash -- a confirmed real orderable part (SF32LB573UB7N6) from SiFli's SF32LB57x ordering table.

parts.name: SF32LB573UB766
parts.summary: QFN68 battery-powered tier with 4MB OPI-PSRAM and 2x asymmetric (16MB + 8MB, 24MB total dual-die) QSPI-NOR Flash -- a confirmed real orderable part (SF32LB573UB766). Its memory code's two Flash digits ('7' and '6') differ, generalizing the dual-die summing rule already established for SF32LB573UB776's matching '77' digits: each Flash digit slot is summed independently rather than requiring a repeat.

parts.name: SF32LB573UB776
parts.summary: QFN68 battery-powered tier with 4MB OPI-PSRAM and 2x 16MB (32MB total dual-die) QSPI-NOR Flash -- a confirmed real orderable part (SF32LB573UB776); its memory code repeats the Flash digit ('77') to indicate two dies of that same capacity, distinguishing it from SF32LB573UB7N6's single 16MB Flash die.

parts.name: SF32LB575UCNN6
parts.summary: QFN68 battery-powered tier with 8MB OPI-PSRAM and no in-package NOR Flash -- a confirmed real orderable part (SF32LB575UCNN6); its 'NN' Flash digits mean none, as in SF32LB577UDNN6.

parts.name: SF32LB577UDNN6
parts.summary: QFN68 battery-powered tier with 16MB OPI-PSRAM and no in-package NOR Flash -- a confirmed real orderable part (SF32LB577UDNN6); designs using this SKU need external Flash via MPI or SDIO.

parts.name: SF32LB57ZUN3N6
parts.summary: QFN68 external-3.3V-powered tier with no in-package PSRAM and 1MB QSPI-NOR Flash only -- a confirmed real orderable part (SF32LB57ZUN3N6), the lowest-memory-configuration 3.3V-supply QFN68 SKU; designs using this SKU need external PSRAM if graphics/UI buffers require it.

parts.name: SF32LB57EYBBN6
parts.summary: QFN80 external-3.3V-powered tier with 2x 4MB (8MB total dual-pool) OPI-PSRAM and no in-package NOR Flash -- a confirmed real orderable part (SF32LB57EYBBN6), the 3.3V-supply QFN80 tier; designs using this SKU need external Flash via MPI or SDIO.

parts.name: SF32LB57GYD7N6
parts.summary: QFN80 external-3.3V-powered tier with 16MB OPI-PSRAM and 16MB QSPI-NOR Flash -- a confirmed real orderable part (SF32LB57GYD7N6), the highest-memory 3.3V-supply QFN80 SKU documented so far.

parts.name: SF32LB57ZVN7N6
parts.summary: BGA112 external-3.3V-powered tier with no co-packaged PSRAM and one 16MB QSPI-NOR Flash die. The unoccupied MPI3 slot leaves the associated BGA112 pins available only as GP static outputs configured through pull-up or pull-down, not as unrestricted GPIOs.

parts.name: SF32LB57GVD776
parts.summary: BGA112 external-3.3V-powered tier with 16MB OPI-PSRAM and 2x 16MB (32MB total dual-die) QSPI-NOR Flash -- a confirmed real orderable part (SF32LB57GVD776), decoded the same way as SF32LB573UB776's repeated Flash digit ('77' = two 128Mb/16MB dies).

parts.name: SF32LB583VCC36
parts.summary: BGA256 tier with 2x 64Mb (16MB) OPI-PSRAM and 1MB QSPI-NOR flash -- mid-tier high-resolution UI designs without moving to the largest HPI-PSRAM tier.

parts.name: SF32LB586VDD36
parts.summary: BGA256 tier with 2x 128Mb (32MB) HPI-PSRAM and 1MB QSPI-NOR flash -- the exact silicon used by SF32LB58-MOD and SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD.

parts.name: SF32LB587VEE56
parts.summary: BGA256 tier with 2x 256Mb (64MB) HPI-PSRAM and 4MB QSPI-NOR flash -- premium wearable, HMI, and edge-AI designs needing the largest local memory headroom.

parts.name: SF32LB58-MOD-N16R16N1
parts.summary: SF32LB58x family-based module (16MB PSRAM tier) lowering BGA256 layout and RF-certification risk while keeping full SF32LB58x-class graphics, storage, and connectivity.

parts.name: SF32LB58-MOD-N16R32N1
parts.summary: SF32LB58x family-based module (32MB PSRAM tier) lowering BGA256 layout and RF-certification risk while keeping full SF32LB58x-class graphics, storage, and connectivity.

parts.name: SF32LB58-MOD-N16R64N4
parts.summary: SF32LB58x family-based module (64MB PSRAM tier) lowering BGA256 layout and RF-certification risk while keeping full SF32LB58x-class graphics, storage, and connectivity.
